subject: Request: latency SLO & term modification for EU inference
messages:
From: Lumenbridge Procurement <procurement@lumenbridge.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@lumenbridge.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request to modify latency target for EU inference

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our engineering team validated Redwood in a short pilot and we like the behavior, but we have one remaining blocker for production: our live inference in the EU region needs a 95th percentile latency closer to 180ms for the 2k token workloads. Your standard contract references a 95th P50/P95 around 300ms for the hosted SKU, which is fine for most customers, but for our use case (real-time decisioning in clinical workflows) the 300ms tail is too long.

We understand dedicated capacity can alter latency but before we sign we need the following clarified in contract language:
- A carve-out SLO of 180ms (P95) for EU inference for the models listed in appendix A (small family).
- A remedy cap that limits service credits to a modest percentage of monthly spend (our procurement typically accepts 2–5%).
- A defined pilot term (initial 3 months) and an option to extend.

Attached is our latency requirement spec (Latency-Requirements-LB.pdf). Please let us know what configuration/pricing you can offer and whether this will need exec approval — we'll loop our legal and procurement once we have an answer.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Senior Procurement Manager
Lumenbridge AI
procurement@lumenbridge.ai

--
Attachment: Latency-Requirements-LB.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@lumenbridge.ai>, Lumenbridge Procurement <procurement@lumenbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request to modify latency target for EU inference

Elena — thanks for sending the requirements and for the honest feedback from your engineers. Appreciated.

Short answer: we can achieve a P95 ~180ms for the specified models, but it requires a Dedicated capacity configuration in the EU region plus a few operational guards. To be explicit about tradeoffs and what we need from Lumenbridge:
- Offer: Dedicated EU pool with reserved capacity sized for your peak QPS; this yields the ~180ms P95 for the listed workloads.
- Pricing/term impact: this is a non-standard SLO; we can offer a 10% onboarding discount for the first 6 months to offset setup and engineering validation.
- Remedy: propose a commercial cap on credits of 3% of monthly invoice and a two-incident cap per billing period for the initial pilot window.
- Pilot: 3 months initial pilot, with telemetry review at weeks 2/6 and an extension option.

This will need deal-desk signoff and an exec clearance because it sets an SLO outside our standard hosted tiers. Marissa — can you prepare a short deal memo and routing for Stephanie? I attached a draft amendment to capture the SLO language (SLA_amendment_draft.docx).

If this direction looks acceptable to you now, I can provision the dedicated test pool next week and run a joint baseline test with your team.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
P: (415) 555-0121

Date: 2026-11-03T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Request to modify latency target for EU inference — deal memo

Team / Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the draft language Jordan. I reviewed the workload profile and the proposed commercial terms. Recommendation from Deal Desk:

1) Approve a 3-month pilot on Dedicated EU capacity with the proposed 180ms P95 for the model family in appendix A.
2) Commercial concessions: 10% onboarding discount (first 6 months) — acceptable.
3) Remedy cap: reduce Jordan's suggested 3% to 2.5% for the initial pilot and limit to two qualifying incidents per monthly billing. After pilot, remedy mechanics revert to standard SLA unless a permanent amendment is approved by Execs + Legal.
4) Operational controls: require Redwood telemetry + Lumenbridge New Relic access (read-only) and an agreed rollback policy (automatic fallback to standard 300ms variant) if stability degrades.
5) Legal: redline amendment for pilot language and an explicit non-precedent clause.

This needs Exec approval because it relaxes our standard public-hosted SLO and sets a capped remedy; requesting Stephanie's signoff. If approved, I will prepare a short executive memo and DocuSign packet for procurement. Deal ID: LMB-2026-014; I attached the one-pager.

Marissa Cole
Senior Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--
Attachment: Deal_Summary_LMB-2026-014.pdf (PDF, 18KB)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@lumenbridge.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Approve: conditional clearance for Lumenbridge pilot (LMB-2026-014)

Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks for the write-up and for keeping the scope tight. I approve the pilot with the following mandatory conditions (no exceptions):

1) Term & scope: 3-month Dedicated EU pilot offering the 180ms P95 target for the specific model family only. Any expansion of scope requires a separate commercial approval.
2) Remedy cap: service credits capped at 3% of monthly invoice (we previously discussed 2.5%; I will accept 3% for the pilot given the strategic nature of the account) and a maximum of two qualifying incidents per billing period during pilot.
3) Discount: 10% off monthly pricing for first 6 months. Discount is limited to this deal and is not reusable for other customers.
4) Telemetry & rollback: Redwood must provide a joint telemetry dashboard (Redwood + read-only New Relic) and agree to an automatic rollback route to the standard 300ms variant if error rate or CPU headroom drops below agreed thresholds.
5) Non-precedent clause: amendment will state this is a limited pilot and shall not set precedence for other customers. Legal to add explicit language.
6) Timebox & acceptance: performance review at week 6; extension only if both sides agree in writing.
7) Execution: procurement must return a PO and signed DocuSign packet by 2026-11-12; otherwise the pilot offer is withdrawn.

Marissa — prepare the DocuSign and Legal redline. Jordan — provision the dedicated test pool and coordinate baseline tests with Elena next Tuesday. Ben — please confirm billing code is set to track the 10% onboarding discount and the remedy cap.

Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
